newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka tea pesticide levels low - standards group.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka tea pesticide levels low - standards group.

text.p: An international tea standards organisation said on Wednesday that only very low levels of pesticide residues had been found in Sri Lankan tea.

The Technical Committee on Tea of the International Organisation for Standardization said at the end of a three-day meeting the issue was not a major concern for Sri Lanka, the world's biggest tea exporter.

"Based on data collected by European Union countries, the meeting concluded that it was not a major concern for Sri Lanka in view of the very low levels of pesticide residues found in Sri Lankan teas," it said in a statement.

Wester Modder, the director of Sri Lanka's Tea Research Institute (TRI), told Reuters in a recent interview that local tea estates had cut the use of pesticides because Western markets were more aware of the dangers of chemicals, which also damage the environment.
"No traces of pesticide have been found in the finished product, though we always get queries, especially from Germany," he said.
The standards committee said it had agreed on methods to estimate the chemical characteristics of green tea and black tea, and determine crude fibre and caffeine content in tea.
It had agreed on international standards for particle size grading of tea.
The meeting also defined international standards for paper sacks for packaging tea, their statement said.
"These standards, which are voluntary, allow those trading in tea to have a reference point in trading," Dr Peter Collier, chairman of the conference, told Reuters.
